The scar's outer boundary — alpha alone against sparser art

Scenario demo-nuke-river-zeta, cells 34,29 to 56,51, ground zero 38,20, AtomicHighYield bands. This window is the beach 21 cells out that the demo's own 05-shore-outer frame is aimed at. Terrain is read from the scenario's map.bin; band membership, the AcceptsSmudgeType gate and ShoreAlphaAt are the engine's. No game was launched.

The ground art is not the tileset. Cells are drawn with real clear1.tem or w1.tem, so Beach and Rock appear as clear ground — the extracted tile cache carries no sand or rock templates. What is exact here is which cells take a scar, at what strength, and from which cut.

1  The boundary

Today — one sprite, ramped alpha

Every scarred cell draws the same art at alpha 0.80–1.00. A cell is the smallest thing that can change, so the waterline is a staircase of square cell edges.

Edge cuts — 25% and 50% of the band

The ramped alpha is unchanged; what differs is that the two cells nearest the water draw thinner cuts of their own variant, so the boundary breaks up into stipple instead of ending on a cell edge.

2  Which cut each cell draws

Not art: this is EdgeSequenceFor evaluated over the real terrain. band's own art 50% cut 25% cut takes no scar outside the disc

Tier field

Alpha field, for comparison

The same cells, as the shore fade sees them. White is full strength. The whole visible range is 0.80 to 1.00 — which is how little there was to see in alpha alone.

3  The gradient, counted

Mean cell luminance by Euclidean distance to the nearest cell that refuses a scar. A boundary that dissolves has a gradient in this column; a boundary that ends on a cell edge does not, however carefully its alpha was ramped.
